overview: Both are protective, often slimy structures bacteria make — but one belongs to a single cell, the other to a whole community.
genZNote: A raincoat versus a whole gated community.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A discrete polysaccharide (occasionally polypeptide) layer surrounding an individual bacterial cell.
aspects.valueB: A structured, surface-attached community of microorganisms embedded in a self-produced extracellular matrix.

aspects.label: Scale / Organization
aspects.valueA: A single-cell structure — every capsulated cell has its own capsule.
aspects.valueB: A multicellular, often multi-species community, sometimes with channels and structural organization.

aspects.label: Composition
aspects.valueA: Usually polysaccharide, tightly and evenly associated with the cell surface.
aspects.valueB: Extracellular polymeric substance (EPS): polysaccharides, proteins, extracellular DNA, and water, loosely surrounding many cells.

aspects.label: Primary Function
aspects.valueA: Anti-phagocytic — helps individual cells evade immune recognition and engulfment.
aspects.valueB: Provides a protected niche: resistance to antibiotics, host defenses, and desiccation for the whole community.

aspects.label: Laboratory Detection
aspects.valueA: Quellung reaction, India ink negative staining, or capsule stains.
aspects.valueB: Crystal violet biofilm assays, confocal microscopy, or visualization on catheters/implants.

aspects.label: Clinical Relevance
aspects.valueA: Key virulence factor in encapsulated pathogens (e.g. Streptococcus pneumoniae, Klebsiella pneumoniae).
aspects.valueB: Central to chronic and device-associated infections (catheters, prosthetic joints, cystic fibrosis lungs).

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueB: Protects a whole embedded community and confers antibiotic tolerance.
